ratings_why.fun: Each tier hands you a new lever (eggs, winders, multipliers, then capstones that join clock and brood), but the board's own bodies stay small until the Herald, so the mid-game growth is mostly invisible Brood.
ratings_why.distinct: 8 over 7 because you plant eggs inside enemy units and race a shared clock that counts both sides' attacks, so reading the next board for who survives three attacks is a placement puzzle no tribe today or generic auto-battler has.

verdict_why: Two small rules gaps (golden Kasimir's gold under Ottilie, and two Bellows beside one unit) need a line each; the shape itself is good.

points.text: Golden Kasimir pays 1 gold per hatched egg, and with Ottilie he lays again at every Chime, so it can be 6 to 8 gold a turn. Say whether only his Start of Combat eggs count, or cap it.
With a Bellows-Hall Tuner on each side of the Herald of Spring, it isn't said whether the effect runs twice, three times or four. Say how two Bellows stack.

Tiers 1 to 4 grow almost only the Brood, which you see only when Chicks hatch. A small permanent tick on the board, such as the Pipit-Moor Hen gaining +1 Health when its egg hatches, would make the early climb visible.
High-Summer Migrant's +1/+1 a turn and half-stats sell is slow for Tier 3. Letting her also gain +1/+1 whenever a Brood bonus lands would make the bank-or-cash-in choice bite sooner.

standouts.why: Little Gernegroß hiding in the enemy and hatching back triple-sized is the seed's joke as one clean, readable swing.
Ottilie is a true capstone: every Hen, Hawk and winder you drafted earlier pays again on the hour.
Frau Wechselbalg turns a tall enemy board against itself and gives a Johnny line with Rohrsang.

weakest.why: Weight-Hanger is a 1/5 whose one effect is a nudge to the clock; it does little on its own at Tier 2.
Old Unruh is a 0/9 that speeds the clock for the enemy too, so it only earns a slot in a full Chime build.
High-Summer Migrant grows slowly and pays out only when sold, so it lags the Tier 3 curve.

flags.note: Herald beside the Bellows gives every Clockwork +4/+4 and the Brood +2/+2 permanently each fight; with two Bellows it may be more. The tribe's main permanent snowball.
Red-Mouth with Ottilie and several Layers is about 12 Heaves a strike. In-fight only, but may end fights in one or two strikes.
Hawk-Barred Hen with Ottilie keeps one enemy dozing all fight; it still hits back, which limits the lock.
Golden Kasimir's gold with Ottilie's repeated lays isn't bounded.
Two Bellows beside one unit: stacking not stated.
